title: Fluid Pressure, Hydraulics and Pneumatics
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Fluid Pressure, Hydraulics and Pneumatics Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe pressure in fluids and how it changes with depth; explain how hydraulic and pneumatic systems use fluids under pressure; assess the environmental and social effects of fluid technologies. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand C: Matter and Energy – Fluids)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 science worksheets on pressure, Pascal's law, hydraulics, pneumatics, submarines and fluid technology. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Fluids pass pressure in all directions; hydraulics use liquids and pneumatics use gases.
body_html:
How to think about it

Pressure is force on an area: pressure = force ÷ area, in pascals (Pa).

  • Pressure in a fluid increases with depth.
  • Pascal's law: pressure on a confined fluid is passed equally in all directions.
  • Hydraulic systems (brakes, excavators) use liquids; pneumatic systems (air brakes, nail guns) use compressed air.
Example

A 200 N force acts on 4 m². What is the pressure?

200 ÷ 4

Answer: 50 Pa

Example

Why are dams thicker at the bottom?

pressure increases with depth

Answer: to hold back the greater pressure

Common mistakes

  • Thinking pressure is the same as force.
  • Thinking liquids are easy to compress.
  • Thinking fluid pressure only pushes down.

faq.a: Hydraulic systems use liquids such as oil. Pneumatic systems use gases such as air.

items.q: How does a hydraulic car lift raise a heavy car with a small force?

items.e: On the Moon your mass is the same, but your weight is less.
